format_reserved.description: genotype, encoded as allele values separated by either of $/$ or $\mid$. The allele values are 0 for the reference allele (what is in the REF field), 1 for the first allele listed in ALT, 2 for the second allele list in ALT and so on. For diploid calls examples could be $0/1$, $1\mid0$, or $1/2$, etc. For haploid calls, e.g.\ on Y, male non-pseudoautosomal X, or mitochondrion, only one allele value should be given; a triploid call might look like $0/0/1$. If a call cannot be made for a sample at a given locus, `.' should be specified for each missing allele in the GT field (for example `$./.$' for a diploid genotype and `.' for haploid genotype). The meanings of the separators are as follows (see the PS field below for more details on incorporating phasing information into the genotypes):
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item GT : genotype, encoded as allele values separated by either of $/$ or $\mid$. The allele values are 0 for the reference allele (what is in the REF field), 1 for the first allele listed in ALT, 2 for the second allele list in ALT and so on. For diploid calls examples could be $0/1$, $1\mid0$, or $1/2$, etc. For haploid calls, e.g.\ on Y, male non-pseudoautosomal X, or mitochondrion, only one allele value should be given; a triploid call might look like $0/0/1$. If a call cannot be made for a sample at a given locus, `.' should be specified for each missing allele in the GT field (for example `$./.$' for a diploid genotype and `.' for haploid genotype). The meanings of the separators are as follows (see the PS field below for more details on incorporating phasing information into the genotypes):

format_reserved.description: sample genotype filter indicating if this genotype was ``called'' (similar in concept to the FILTER field). Again, use PASS to indicate that all filters have been passed, a semicolon-separated list of codes for filters that fail, or `.' to indicate that filters have not been applied. These values should be described in the meta-information in the same way as FILTERs (String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted)

Again, use PASS to indicate that all filters have been passed, a semicolon-separated list of codes for filters that fail, or `.' to indicate that filters have not been applied. These values should be described in the meta-information in the same way as FILTERs (String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted)

format_reserved.description: genotype likelihoods comprised of comma separated floating point $log_{10}$-scaled likelihoods for all possible genotypes given the set of alleles defined in the REF and ALT fields. In presence of the GT field the same ploidy is expected and the canonical order is used; without GT field, diploidy is assumed. If A is the allele in REF and B,C,... are the alleles as ordered in ALT, the ordering of genotypes for the likelihoods is given by: F(j/k) = (k*(k+1)/2)+j. In other words, for biallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB; for triallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB,AC,BC,CC, etc. For example: GT:GL 0/1:-323.03,-99.29,-802.53 (Floats)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item GL : genotype likelihoods comprised of comma separated floating point $log_{10}$-scaled likelihoods for all possible genotypes given the set of alleles defined in the REF and ALT fields. In presence of the GT field the same ploidy is expected and the canonical order is used; without GT field, diploidy is assumed. If A is the allele in REF and B,C,... are the alleles as ordered in ALT, the ordering of genotypes for the likelihoods is given by: F(j/k) = (k*(k+1)/2)+j.  In other words, for biallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB; for triallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB,AC,BC,CC, etc.  For example: GT:GL 0/1:-323.03,-99.29,-802.53 (Floats)

format_reserved.description: genotype likelihoods of heterogeneous ploidy, used in presence of uncertain copy number. For example: GLE=0:-75.22,1:-223.42,0/0:-323.03,1/0:-99.29,1/1:-802.53 (String)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item GLE : genotype likelihoods of heterogeneous ploidy, used in presence of uncertain copy number. For example: GLE=0:-75.22,1:-223.42,0/0:-323.03,1/0:-99.29,1/1:-802.53 (String)

format_reserved.description: the phred-scaled genotype likelihoods rounded to the closest integer (and otherwise defined precisely as the GL field) (Integers)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item PL : the phred-scaled genotype likelihoods rounded to the closest integer (and otherwise defined precisely as the GL field) (Integers)

format_reserved.description: the phred-scaled genotype posterior probabilities (and otherwise defined precisely as the GL field); intended to store imputed genotype probabilities (Floats)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item GP : the phred-scaled genotype posterior probabilities (and otherwise defined precisely as the GL field); intended to store imputed genotype probabilities (Floats)

format_reserved.description: conditional genotype quality, encoded as a phred quality $-10log_{10}$ p(genotype call is wrong, conditioned on the site's being variant) (Integer)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item GQ : conditional genotype quality, encoded as a phred quality $-10log_{10}$ p(genotype call is wrong, conditioned on the site's being variant) (Integer)

format_reserved.description: haplotype qualities, two comma separated phred qualities (Integers)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item HQ : haplotype qualities, two comma separated phred qualities (Integers)

format_reserved.description: phase set. A phase set is defined as a set of phased genotypes to which this genotype belongs. Phased genotypes for an individual that are on the same chromosome and have the same PS value are in the same phased set. A phase set specifies multi-marker haplotypes for the phased genotypes in the set. All phased genotypes that do not contain a PS subfield are assumed to belong to the same phased set. If the genotype in the GT field is unphased, the corresponding PS field is ignored. The recommended convention is to use the position of the first variant in the set as the PS identifier (although this is not required). (Non-negative 32-bit Integer)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item PS : phase set.  A phase set is defined as a set of phased genotypes to which this genotype belongs.  Phased genotypes for an individual that are on the same chromosome and have the same PS value are in the same phased set.  A phase set specifies multi-marker haplotypes for the phased genotypes in the set.  All phased genotypes that do not contain a PS subfield are assumed to belong to the same phased set.  If the genotype in the GT field is unphased, the corresponding PS field is ignored.  The recommended convention is to use the position of the first variant in the set as the PS identifier (although this is not required). (Non-negative 32-bit Integer)

format_reserved.description: phasing quality, the phred-scaled probability that alleles are ordered incorrectly in a heterozygote (against all other members in the phase set). We note that we have not yet included the specific measure for precisely defining ``phasing quality''; our intention for now is simply to reserve the PQ tag for future use as a measure of phasing quality. (Integer)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item PQ : phasing quality, the phred-scaled probability that alleles are ordered incorrectly in a heterozygote (against all other members in the phase set).  We note that we have not yet included the specific measure for precisely defining ``phasing quality''; our intention for now is simply to reserve the PQ tag for future use as a measure of phasing quality. (Integer)

format_reserved.description: comma separated list of expected alternate allele counts for each alternate allele in the same order as listed in the ALT field (typically used in association analyses) (Integers)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item EC : comma separated list of expected alternate allele counts for each alternate allele in the same order as listed in the ALT field (typically used in association analyses) (Integers)

format_reserved.description: RMS mapping quality, similar to the version in the INFO field. (Integer)
format_reserved.raw_source_line: \item MQ : RMS mapping quality, similar to the version in the INFO field. (Integer)

VCFv4.4.table_form: Longtable reserved INFO and FORMAT tables.

VCFv4.1_to_4.2.finding: VCFv4.2 explicitly adds the '*' allele for an allele missing due to an upstream deletion; the VCFv4.1 ALT list does not include it.
Both versions present reserved INFO and FORMAT fields as prose enumerations rather than Number/Type tables; do not retroactively assign later table Number/Type values.

VCFv4.2_to_4.3.finding: VCFv4.3 presents reserved INFO and FORMAT definitions in tables with Number and Type columns; the 4.1/4.2 prose lists do not contain those columns.
VCFv4.3 reserved INFO table records END as Number=1 Integer and describes end position on CHROM for symbolic alleles; its interpretation must be read with the subsequent symbolic-allele section.
VCFv4.3 FORMAT table has the core AD/ADF/ADR/DP/EC/FT/GL/GP/GQ/GT/HQ/MQ/PL/PP/PQ/PS set; no PSL/PSO/PSQ rows.

VCFv4.3_to_4.4.finding: The INFO reserved table rows, Number, Type and descriptions are unchanged in the source table inventory between 4.3 and 4.4.
VCFv4.4 adds PSL (Number=P, String), PSO (Number=P, Integer), and PSQ (Number=P, Integer) to the FORMAT reserved table; VCFv4.3 has PS but not these three rows.

VCFv4.4_to_4.5.finding: VCFv4.5 adds LA/LAA and local-allele equivalents LAD/LADF/LADR/LEC/LGL/LGP/LPL/LPP; the table rows must be interpreted jointly with LAA prose and BCF empty-vector caveats.
VCFv4.5 adds M/DPM/ADM base-modification key families and aliases, with Number=M and strand-aware interpretation; no such rows appear in 4.4 reserved FORMAT table.

VCFv4.5 contains explicit arbitrary-ploidy genotype-ordering pseudocode and allele-level phasing indicators; earlier versions' diploid triangular formula and genotype-level separator description must not be silently treated as identical.

review_findings: The source format itself is versioned: 4.1/4.2 enumerate reserved fields in prose and 4.3/4.4 introduce explicit Number/Type tables. The ledger must preserve which attributes were actually specified in each version.
The 4.1 and 4.2 reserved INFO enumerations contain 18 entries; their FORMAT enumerations are prose lists, not Number/Type tables.
The 4.3 and 4.4 reserved INFO tables each contain 21 rows; FORMAT tables differ by the three phase-set-list fields added in 4.4.
Do not assign 4.5 local-allele or base-modification definitions to 4.1–4.4 without source evidence.
GT separator subitems (slash and vertical bar) were separated from the FORMAT reserved-field inventory; they define GT semantics and are not independent FORMAT keys.
